summary: Iteration 4 — TOTP MFA + security-question + password-reset end-to-end verification. Backend: 82/82 pytest passing (14 new MFA cases in /app/backend/tests/test_mfa_auth.py + 51 existing compass + 17 existing household-centric, all updated to flow through MFA). Frontend (Playwright): multi-step login verified for seeded advisor (mfa_required -> dashboard), wrong password stays on password step, wrong TOTP code stays on mfa step, forgot/reset flow renders security question and accepts answer=toronto+TOTP, newly-registered Solo user hits mfa_setup (QR + secret shown), scanning the on-page secret -> security-question step -> dashboard, and subsequent login uses mfa_required (no QR). /api/auth/me response verified to NOT contain mfa_secret or security_answer_hash. Previous iteration's react-query cross-tenant cache leak is CONFIRMED FIXED (AuthContext now calls qc.clear() in both login and logout).
critical_code_review_comments: server.py reset-password: when user.mfa_enabled is False (e.g. a user who registered but has not yet enrolled TOTP) the code field is ignored. This is intentional per spec (`if user.get('mfa_enabled') and not verify_totp`) but worth noting — a user who registered but never logged in has no security question yet, so forgot-password returns {question:null,mfa:false} and reset-password will fail at the security-answer check anyway, which closes the hole.

login() returns status code 200 for 'mfa_required' / 'mfa_setup' intermediate states instead of a dedicated code (e.g. 202). Fine, but any legacy consumer that keyed off a bare {token} will silently break (updated our regression suite to handle both).

mfa/verify consumes the challenge token but does not blacklist it on success — the same challenge+code pair can be replayed inside the 10-min window. Low risk because codes rotate every 30s, but a one-shot nonce would be belt+braces.

reset-password does not invalidate/rotate any active sessions after a password reset. A compromised token would survive the owner's own reset. Consider bumping a `tokens_valid_after` timestamp per user and checking it in get_current_user.

security-question setup accepts any string for `question` from the client — no server-side validation that it matches one of SECURITY_QUESTIONS. Not exploitable (user is just hurting themselves) but adding `if body.question not in SECURITY_QUESTIONS: raise 400` would prevent typos locking users out.
DEMO_TOTP_SECRET is shared across all seeded users. Fine for a demo but must be removed before any production seed.
